??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Welcome to the clinic. It's an awning, a cabinet and a kettle, but the kettle's very good. Rooftop tumble? Burnt fingers? Or just passing?
    - *Player*. The toad salve is a marvel. Cools a burn before you've finished saying ow. Tinder has stopped pretending not to use it.
    - *Player*. Fewer tusk wounds this month. Not none. Fewer. Patch and I drank a very small toast to that, out of the medicine cups.
    - What can I do for you?
        - *Choice:* How did you become a healer?
        - *Choice:* Who comes to the clinic?
        - *Choice:* Why music, while you stitch?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. I'm well.
    - By failing at something else. I came up from the orchards outside Kaldemor at nineteen to be a singer. I was not a good singer. I was, it turned out, a good holder of people's hands while Henna Bright stitched them.
    - Henna kept this awning for thirty years. She taught me everything and called me 'the tenor' until the day she died. She left me the awning, the cabinet and the kettle. I patched the awning green. She'd have hated the colour.
    - Rooftop tumbles, mostly. Burnt fingers from the Row. Tinder, often. Splinters I send to Patch at the Gate Walk, and she sends me the stitches. We share supplies when we have any.
    - Lately, more and more travellers hurt on the roads. Bites, tusks, falls. The bandages and salves that come in from outside are scarce. I'm making more of my own, and Crow sells tonics that might be anything, because the bottles say nothing.
    - Nobody can hum and panic at the same time. Try it. You can't. So I ask a patient for their favourite tune, and by the second verse I'm tying off the last stitch. The singer in me never got a stage. It got a stool under an awning. That's enough.
    - Mind how you go. And if you do fall off something, fall toward the awning.
